title: DSP Pension Fund NPS Review: Returns, Portfolio, and Fees (2026)
description: DSP Pension Fund, a relatively new entrant, manages investments under the National Pension System (NPS). It offers both Active and Auto Choice options for sub.

faq.q: What is the National Pension System (NPS)?
faq.a: NPS is a voluntary, long-term retirement savings scheme managed by the PFRDA, designed to enable subscribers to make systematic contributions during their working life to secure their future post-retirement.

faq.q: How does DSP Pension Fund fit into NPS?
faq.a: DSP Pension Fund is one of the Pension Fund Managers (PFMs) appointed by PFRDA to manage the contributions of NPS subscribers across various asset classes like equity, corporate debt, and government securities.

faq.q: Can I switch my Pension Fund Manager to or from DSP Pension Fund?
faq.a: Yes, NPS subscribers have the flexibility to switch their Pension Fund Manager (PFM) once in a financial year. This can be done online through the NPS portal.

faq.q: What are the main investment options offered by DSP Pension Fund?
faq.a: DSP Pension Fund offers both Active Choice, where you decide your asset allocation, and Auto Choice (Life Cycle Funds) where allocation automatically adjusts with age, across Equity (E), Corporate Debt (C), and Government Securities (G) schemes.

faq.q: Are the fees for DSP Pension Fund high?
faq.a: No, the fees charged by all Pension Fund Managers under NPS, including DSP Pension Fund, are very low and are regulated by the PFRDA, making NPS a cost-effective retirement savings option.

faq.q: What is the significance of "most AA-rated corporate bonds" in DSP's portfolio?
faq.a: Holding the most AA-rated corporate bonds indicates a conservative approach within the corporate debt segment, prioritising credit quality and lower default risk, which might lead to relatively stable but potentially lower returns compared to funds taking higher credit risk.

faq.q: How does DSP Pension Fund's equity performance compare to peers?
faq.a: Recent data suggests that DSP Pension Fund has recorded the weakest 1-year equity returns among its peers, which is a point of consideration for subscribers with high equity exposure.
